subject: Aligning invoice cadence to annual prepay + bridge credit proposal
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@astrolytics.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.malhotra@astrolytics.com, tom.contracts@astrolytics.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning invoice cadence to annual prepay + bridge credit proposal

Thanks for the note, Irene — appreciate the quick turnaround on the numbers. A few questions from our side after reviewing the spreadsheet: 

- We currently operate on monthly OPEX and the CFO is hesitant to move all spend to upfront CAPEX. Is there a structure where we can preserve monthly recognition while still giving Redwood an upfront commitment (e.g., annual prepay paid in quarterly tranches)?
- If we move to a 3-yr prepay, what guardrails exist if our usage grows faster than the ramp (we expect a 60% QoQ increase in Q1 after production)?
- What does the true-up process look like and when would credits be applied?

Also looping in Tom from contracts to understand any termination/ETC exposure. Happy to hop on a short call if helpful — Alex

--
Alex Gomez
Director of ML Platforms, Astrolytics
alex.gomez@astrolytics.com

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@astrolytics.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning invoice cadence to annual prepay + bridge credit proposal

Alex — thanks for the thoughtful questions. High level responses inline, and I attached an updated pricing_model_v3.xlsx with two alternative payment profiles (A and B): one fully prepaid annually and one hybrid quarterly-paid prepay.

- Quarterly-tranche option: We can accept the annual prepay commitment collected in four equal tranches (due at the start of each quarter). This preserves partial monthly recognition for your finance team while giving Redwood committed revenue. There is a modest premium to tranche the payment (approx +2.5% dealer fee built into the model) to cover capacity reservation and early billing overhead.

- Ramp overruns: For 3-year deals we propose a dynamic step-up credit: if usage exceeds the agreed ramp by >25% in any rolling quarter, we bill overage at the committed unit rate up to 150% of committed consumption, then at a 15% premium beyond that. If usage growth permanently exceeds expected trajectory, we do a mid-term uplift evaluation at the 12-month mark to re-baseline pricing and capacity.

- True-up timing: Quarterly true-ups with refundable prepay credits applied within 30 days of quarter close. Credits can be left as account balance or used to offset future tranches. For annual reconciliation we allow one true-up within the first 6 months tied to initial production variance.

Next steps I suggest: (1) pick either profile A (annual upfront) or B (quarterly tranche prepay) in the XLS, (2) agree on a 12-month ramp baseline (we propose 0 -> 40% -> 70% -> 100% over first year) and any pilot offset, (3) review SOW for usage definitions and SLA attachment.

I can make time Thursday AM for a 30-min pricing / finance sync with Alex + Tom.

Thanks,
Irene
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
[attachment: pricing_model_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: tom.contracts@astrolytics.com

Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning invoice cadence to annual prepay + bridge credit proposal

Irene — quick from legal/finance: 

- Term & ETAs: Astrolytics prefers a 36-month term but will not accept large early termination penalties. Can Redwood offer graduated termination protection (e.g., 6 months revenue prorated year 1; 4 months year 2; 2 months year 3) instead of a flat ETC?
- Accounting treatment: If we opt for quarterly-tranche prepay, we need a clear schedule of deliverables / capacity reservations in the SOW so our accounting team can allocate appropriately.
- Pilot offset: we are pushing to have a 3-month pilot with usage credit that offsets month 1 of tranche 1. Is that acceptable?

Also, can you confirm whether the step-up premium applies immediately at point-of-overage or only after a mid-term uplift?

Thanks,
Tom (Contracts)
Astrolytics
[attachment: Astrolytics_Finance_Qs.pdf (pdf stub)]

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: tom.contracts@astrolytics.com, alex.gomez@astrolytics.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning invoice cadence to annual prepay + bridge credit proposal

Tom / Alex — appreciate the detailed asks. Proposed concessions below (summary and action items):

Summary concessions we can provide:
- Payment cadence: Offer Profile B (quarterly-tranche prepay) with a reduced tranche premium of +1.5% (down from 2.5%) if Astrolytics signs within 14 days.
- ET termination: Graduated ETC as requested: prorated 6/4/2 months across years 1/2/3. No carve-outs for overage billing.
- Pilot offset: Grant a 3-month pilot credit equal to the estimated Q1 usage (applied as a deduction to tranche 1). If you migrate to full annual up-front later, the pilot credit will convert to account balance.
- Overage / step-up: Immediate overage billing applies at the committed rate up to 150%. Beyond 150% we apply a 15% premium. We also propose a mid-term uplift evaluation at month 12 if sustained >120% run-rate.

Operational asks from Redwood:
- Finalize baseline ramp numbers (I recommend we use Astrolytics' internal forecast table in the XLS as the baseline).
- Sign SOW with explicit "capacity reservation" clause and quarterly true-up schedule.
- Finance to confirm acceptance of quarterly-tranche billing code on the PO (we will provide invoice templates).

Attached revised SOW + term summary for signature. Mark (legal) is copied for any final redlines. If everyone is aligned I will route for signature and schedule a Friday 11am PT pricing walk to lock numbers.

Best,
Irene
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
